newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-DALY WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. OPEN WITHOUT EXPLANATION.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DALY WITHDRAWS FROM U.S. OPEN WITHOUT EXPLANATION.

text.p: John Daly, the troubled golfer who has been trying to recover from alcohol and gambling problems, withdrew from the U.S. Open without explanation on Friday, halfway through his round.

Daly, who shot seven-over-par 77 in Thursday's first round of the Open at Congressional Country Club, played the first nine holes of his second round in three over par early Friday morning before suddenly walking off the course.

The winner of the 1995 British Open and the 1991 PGA Championship, Daly underwent substance abuse treatment in April after an alcohol-related incident in his hotel room after a night of drinking during the Players Championship.
He also withdrew from that event and subsequently underwent treatment at the Betty Ford Clinic.
That episode cost Daly several lucrative endorsement contracts but he has since singned with Callaway Golf -- with the understanding that he continues counselling.
It was the second time that Daly, 31, had undergone treatment for alcohol abuse since he burst on the golf scene with a surprising victory in the 1991 PGA at Crooked Stick in Carmel, Indiana.

Daly did not offer any explanation for his withdrawal from the Open here. He apparently did not even tell his caddie, who waited on the 10th tee for the player, but Daly just walked off the course after nine holes and left the club grounds.
